morning_soundtrack.title: Bonnie “Prince” Billy & Linus Announce Jules de Corte Tribute Album, Share Three Songs
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Up until this very afternoon, I'd never heard of Jules de Corte, a blind Dutch singer-songwriter who won some European prizes in the '60s and who died in 1996 at the age of 71. I'd also never heard of the improvisational Belgian quartet Linus. I had, however, heard of beloved roots-music weirdo Bonnie "Prince" Billy, so the news that he's making a Jules de Corte tribute album with Linus demanded further investigation.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The musical equivalent of stumbling into a dusty foreign-language record shop and leaving two hours later with something you never knew you needed.

morning_soundtrack.title: Shane Parish Surprise Releases New Album Dental Work To Pay For His Dental Work
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Six-string master Shane Parish has been in these (web)pages a fair amount in recent years, both for acoustic ventures like translating Autechre and Aphex Twin songs to guitar and electric pursuits like the Bill Orcutt Guitar Quartet . We also caught up with him last month at Philadelphia's Making Time ∞ festival , where it seems he was dealing with some health concerns. As a result, there's a new surprise Shane Parish album out today.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The scrappy, bittersweet sound of turning a bad situation into something quietly brilliant — art made out of necessity, with teeth.

morning_soundtrack.title: Alex Lahey Shares Previously Unreleased Songs On Garage Sale [Vol. 1] EP
morning_soundtrack.snippet: In 2023, Alexa Lahey released her latest album The Answer Is Always Yes . Since then, the Australian singer-songwriter has shared a deluxe version , as well as some songs and collaborations , including one with Tegan And Sara . Now, she's back with the Garage Sale [Vol. 1] EP.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Like flipping through a cardboard box of unlabeled cassettes at a yard sale and finding a hidden gem between the couch cushions.

morning_soundtrack.title: BONUS TRACKS: 39 Bob Dylan CDs, New Anti-ICE Compilation, and More Roots Music News
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Columbia Records and Legacy Recordings announced a massive new Bob Dylan box set titled T he Rolling Thunder Revue: The 1976 Live Recordings due out November 6. Distributed via 39 CDs, the 371 tracks that have never been head on recordings before from 19 shows, mostly across the southern states.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The thrill of cracking open a time capsule — road dust, cigarette smoke, and 39 discs worth of American myth spilling out all at once.

morning_soundtrack.title: David Sylvian Sets New Album The Distance Between the Killer and the Killing
morning_soundtrack.snippet: His first proper new LP since 2009 compiles improvisational sessions recorded between 2012 and 2025 into one 46-minute instrumental
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The sound of a long silence finally broken — hushed, searching, and heavy with everything left unsaid across sixteen years.

morning_soundtrack.title: Zach Bryan Wears “Free Palestine” Shirt During Show at Gillette Stadium
morning_soundtrack.snippet: The fashion statement came weeks after Bob Kraft led a campaign to get Macklemore kicked off Ed Sheeran's tour. Zach Bryan Wears “Free Palestine” Shirt During Show at Gillette Stadium Alex Young
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: A stadium full of charged air and held breath, where a T-shirt suddenly carries more weight than the setlist.

morning_soundtrack.title: Dave Grohl Lives Out Boyhood Dream by Joining AC/DC for “Highway to Hell”
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Grohl's Foo Fighters served as the surprise opener for AC/DC's show at MetLife Stadium. Dave Grohl Lives Out Boyhood Dream by Joining AC/DC for “Highway to Hell” Alex Young
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Pure fist-pumping, chest-swelling catharsis — the moment a kid's bedroom poster becomes a sweaty, roaring reality.

morning_soundtrack.title: AOC and Bernie Sanders Introduce The Strokes Prior to NYC Show
morning_soundtrack.snippet: "The greatest city in the world is now welcoming the greatest rock band of our generation." AOC and Bernie Sanders Introduce The Strokes Prior to NYC Show Alex Young
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The electric crackle of a city that still believes, against all odds, in the union of rock and roll and righteous anger.

morning_soundtrack.title: The Album Leaf’s Ambient Music Finds Its Perfect Voice
morning_soundtrack.snippet: After 25 years of creating enthralling ambient instrumental music, the Album Leaf has found singers who understand how to speak its language.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Like stepping into a fog-softened morning where, for once, every sound feels like it was placed there just for you.

morning_soundtrack.title: Midori Hirano Draws Inspiration from a Classic Icelandic Film
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Midori Hirano's The Juniper Tree is fascinated by humans' place in the natural world. She has successfully found a sonic outlet for this sense of wonder
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Standing barefoot in a Nordic forest at dusk, feeling simultaneously very small and quietly held by something ancient.

morning_soundtrack.title: Carly Rae Jepsen Finds Life’s Balance on ‘Day and Night’
morning_soundtrack.snippet: On Day and Night , Carly Rae Jepsen blends funk, synths, and acoustics for an eclectic but cohesive collection of tunes about love, loss, and settling down.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Catching the last warm light of an afternoon that somehow contains both heartbreak and the very real possibility of dancing through it.

global_silver_linings.title: UK’s National Museums to Continue 25-Year Policy of Free Entry for Foreign Visitors
global_silver_linings.snippet: After months of discussions between UK ministries, the tourism sector, and London’s museums, the government has decided that the country’s national museums will remain free to international visitors. These 14 institutions include such renowned museums as the National Gallery, the British Museum, and the Natural History Museum among others, which together attract tens of millions […]
global_silver_linings.reason: Britain's commitment to keeping its national museums free for all visitors — regardless of where they're from — is a quiet but powerful statement that culture and history belong to everyone. After 25 years, this policy continues to put human connection above profit.

global_silver_linings.title: Want your home to be ‘the house’ for your teens? Mom shares her 4 secret tricks.
global_silver_linings.snippet: There are so many benefits to being "the house" for your teens. Here's how to do it.
global_silver_linings.reason: A parent sharing hard-won wisdom on how to create a welcoming home for teenagers is a small but meaningful reminder that community can start right at your own front door. When young people have a safe place to gather, good things tend to follow.

discovery_articles.title: Queer Arts Featured in San Francisco, California
discovery_articles.snippet: The storefront where Harvey Milk sold film and strategized his historic run for San Francisco supervisor has found a fitting second act. Today it's home to Queer Arts Featured, better known as Queer AF: part gallery, part boutique, and part community gathering space for queer artists who are tired of waiting for someone else's invitation. Rather than freezing the space as a shrine, the founders keep it buzzing with rotating exhibitions, open mics, gender-affirming clothing swaps, and craft nights.
discovery_articles.ferns_note: Harvey Milk's old camera shop could have become a museum frozen in amber, but instead it kept his spirit — restless, practical, political — fully alive. There's something quietly radical about a space that honors a legacy by refusing to be precious about it.

discovery_articles.title: The Abandoned Monorail of Melaka in Melaka, Malaysia
discovery_articles.snippet: Several monorail systems were built in Malaysia in the 2000s, and while quite a few no longer exist, the one in Kuala Lumpur still runs and is popular. In 2008 in Melaka, the decision was made to build a monorail system as part of a development called 'The Shore', which was a residential, shopping, and commercial complex on the banks of the Melaka river, which includes the city's tallest building. Construction began in 2008 and finished in 2010 at a cost of RM16.5 million (roughly £3m or $4.1m).
discovery_articles.ferns_note: Built for RM16.5 million and retired almost immediately, Melaka's monorail stands as a monument to the particular hubris of optimistic development projections. It's the ghost of a commute that never happened, haunting the skyline of a city that simply moved on without it.

discovery_articles.title: Google Wants to Send Data Centers to Space—and Just Launched an Experimental Satellite to Test Whether Its Ambitious Plan Will Work
discovery_articles.snippet: The tech giant aims to use the near-constant sunlight available in low-Earth orbit to power data centers. The experimental satellite, launched October 1, holds four computer chips that can run Google’s Gemini A.I. for 15 minutes at a time
discovery_articles.ferns_note: The quiet strangeness here is that four computer chips are currently orbiting Earth, running an AI for fifteen minutes at a stretch like a very expensive thought experiment. We've gone from server farms to server satellites, and somehow that happened between lunch and dinner.

discovery_articles.title: Scientists Discover Two New Species of Sea Spider in the Pacific Northwest—and They Look Like They Came Straight Out of a Horror Movie
discovery_articles.snippet: You don't need to worry about the critters coming after you, since they're only a fraction of an inch across. They join the roughly 1,400 known species of ocean-dwelling spiders
discovery_articles.ferns_note: Sea spiders already number 1,400 known species, living their horror-movie lives largely unnoticed in the deep — and we're still finding new ones, fraction-of-an-inch at a time. The ocean's capacity for quietly keeping secrets continues to be genuinely unsettling.

discovery_articles.title: An Arson Investigation Is Underway After a Suspected ‘Senseless Act of Vandalism’ Destroys a Newly Installed Benjamin Harrison Statue
discovery_articles.snippet: The 3D-printed piece was created by students and faculty at Indiana University Indianapolis and had been installed on September 16
discovery_articles.ferns_note: Benjamin Harrison is arguably America's most overlooked president, so there's a grim irony in the fact that the moment someone finally made a statue for him, it was set on fire within weeks. Some obscurities, it seems, are fiercely defended.

discovery_articles.title: A New Exhibition Spotlights 4,500 Years of Broken, Shot-Up and Degraded Artworks to Explore the ‘Power of the Fragment’
discovery_articles.snippet: The show, on view in Florence and coming to D.C. next year, examines the history and impact of destroyed sculptures throughout time and across cultures
discovery_articles.ferns_note: A broken sculpture isn't a failure of preservation — it's often the most honest record of everything history has felt strongly enough to attack. This exhibition makes the radical argument that a chipped nose or a toppled torso tells us more than any intact masterpiece ever could.

featured_read.title: Your Immune System Ages in Two Big Bursts
featured_read.snippet: Your 40s and 60s are periods of intense remodeling
featured_read.blurb: It turns out your immune system doesn't age gradually — it lurches through two dramatic renovations, one in your forties and one in your sixties, which reframes a lot of what we think we know about midlife health. This piece makes those invisible upheavals feel suddenly, urgently legible.

reading_room.title: Journaling to remember
reading_room.snippet: By cataloguing the ephemera that slip between the headlines of my days, future me has a ready reckoner of my life - by Anandi Mishra Read on Psyche
reading_room.blurb: Anandi Mishra makes a quiet case for recording not the big moments but the small atmospheric ones — the receipts, the offhand remarks, the particular light — as the truest archive of a life. It's a gentle argument for paying better attention to your own days before they dissolve.

reading_room.title: On Children’s Books: Faith Ringgold’s The Invisible Princess
reading_room.snippet: Asha Futterman, whose poem “Study of Children” appears in our new Fall issue, on the unsettling harmony of Faith Ringgold’s 1998 fairy tale.
reading_room.blurb: Faith Ringgold's 1998 fairy tale holds a harmony that Asha Futterman calls unsettling, and this essay earns that word by sitting with what children's books can carry that adult literature rarely dares. A small book, it turns out, can hold enormous weight.

reading_room.title: Behind His Great Novels, an Unbearable Family Secret
reading_room.snippet: "The Irish author Sebastian Barry has made a career of mining his family history. But he kept one story buried."
reading_room.blurb: Sebastian Barry has spent decades excavating his family's hidden histories in fiction, but one story he couldn't bring himself to touch — until now. This Longreads piece follows the unbearable thing he kept buried and what it cost him to finally surface it.

reading_room.title: Audible has a creepy new feature that lets you talk to characters in books.
reading_room.snippet: Ever wanted to crack the creme bruleé of Mr. Darcy’s stoicism? Or give Humbert Humbert a piece of your mind? If so, you’re in luck.
reading_room.blurb: Audible's new feature lets you hold actual conversations with literary characters, which sounds whimsical until you sit with what it means to make Humbert Humbert interactive and monetizable. This piece asks the quietly troubling question of what we lose when fiction learns to talk back.

reading_room.title: Why Americans Stopped Throwing Dinner Parties
reading_room.snippet: The share of adults who say they regularly have friends over has declined dramatically since 1975.
reading_room.blurb: The American dinner party didn't just fall out of fashion — it collapsed, and this Atlantic essay traces the social, architectural, and psychological reasons we stopped inviting people over for an evening and never quite started again. It reads less like a trend piece and more like a quiet eulogy for a particular kind of intimacy.

garden_note.note: First light nudges over the Zürichberg just before seven, catching the last of the dahlias in that amber-edged way only October knows how to manage — drink it in before the mist decides otherwise. The garden is easing into its quieter self now, and there's a particular satisfaction in working alongside it rather than against it.
in_season: Dahlias — cut the last blooms before the first hard frost claims them
Quince — harvest when fully golden and fragrant on the branch
Plant tulip and allium bulbs while the soil still holds warmth
Rake and compost fallen leaves before they mat the lawn

news.title: 45 Best Thanksgiving Side Dishes That Travel Exceptionally Well
news.snippet: If your Thanksgiving involves hopping on the train or settling in for an hour-long car ride, fret not — there are plenty of cold side dishes that can stand up to the journey. If you need to bring a cold side that can be prepared in advance and ready to hit the table as is, we have plenty of options that travel well. From crunchy slaws and nutty grains to hearty roasted salads (including Jennifer Garner’s exclusive recipe!
news.blurb: A thoughtful guide for the holiday cook who also happens to be a passenger — because nobody should have to choose between a beautiful side dish and a comfortable commute.

news.title: The Best Food Advent Calendars of 2026 (Yes, They’re Already Here)
news.snippet: During the holiday season, most of us are so focused on buying gifts for other people that we don’t spend enough time treating ourselves. An advent calendar is an especially festive way to surprise yourself with something nice each of the anticipatory days leading up to Christmas, and it’s even better when you get to […]
news.blurb: Advent calendars filled with actual food rather than waxy chocolate are proof that the season's best gift is, and always has been, the one you quietly keep for yourself.

news.title: Henry Harris’s recipe for vegetarian endive au gratin
news.snippet: A worthy, meat-free version of the best comfort dish ever, this French classic is best served with a chilled red and a crisp salad This is the best comfort dish on planet Earth. Cauliflower cheese held that title when I was a child, but I still remember the first time I ate this gratin, made by Simon Hopkinson at his restaurant Hilaire in London, and wanting to take it away and eat it in a quiet corner. Endive when braised well retains a gentle bitterness that contrasts beautifully with a cheese-heavy bechamel.
news.blurb: A French classic gone gloriously meat-free — Henry Harris's endive au gratin makes a compelling case that the best comfort dish on earth might just be wearing a new hat.

recipe.title: Thin & Crispy (3-Minute) Chicken Cutlets
recipe.snippet: Thin & Crispy (3-Minute) Chicken Cutlets If you hate the typical three-step breading station required to make chicken cutlets, this recipe is for you. If you hate pounding chicken breasts, this recipe is also for you. Read on to learn the secret to making thin, crispy, and completely delicious chicken cutlets — the easy way!
recipe.blurb: Golden, shatteringly crisp, and on the table in three minutes flat, these chicken cutlets are the weeknight hero that asks almost nothing of you and delivers everything in return.

fern_data.greeting: Wednesday has that particular quality of not quite being anything yet. Today's edition leans into the unresolved: Shane Parish sold an album to pay for dental work, David Sylvian named his new record after the gap between a killer and a killing, and your immune system, it turns out, ages in sudden lurches rather than quietly.
